name: Nonrelativistic hydrogen levels E_n = -m alpha^2/(2n^2) and <r>_{n,l} = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m alpha)

source.located: Primary: Schrodinger, Ann. Phys. 79 (1926) 361 (levels); <r>_{nl} via Waller Z. Phys. 38 (1926) 635 / Pasternack PNAS 23 (1937) 91 / Kramers 1938 -- none on arXiv. Read via restatement in: arXiv:0707.1887 (Suslov & Trey, J. Math. Phys. 49 (2008) 012104) p.8-11 eqs (3.1)-(3.5), (3.13)-(3.15), p.16 eqs (4.16)-(4.17); arXiv:0908.0032 (Cordero-Soto & Suslov 2009) p.2 eqs (2.6)-(2.7); arXiv:2409.03787 (CODATA 2022) p.10-11 eqs (26), (28)-(31), p.15 eq (50), Tables IV, XXXII, XXXIII.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text for all three arXiv papers (and 1807.08337, 2602.14980 for later literature). Schrodinger 1926, Waller 1926, Pasternack 1937 and Kramers 1938 are NAMED-NOT-READ; the formulas are taken from Suslov-Trey eqs (3.5) and (3.15), which agree with Cordero-Soto-Suslov eq (2.6)-(2.7), with CODATA eq (26) at F = 0, and with excite.py:953-958.

published_statement: Suslov & Trey (0707.1887 p.8-9): 'The nonrelativistic Coulomb wave functions ... are psi_nlm = R_nl(r) Y_lm, R_nl = (2/n^2)(Z/a0)^{3/2} sqrt((n-l-1)!/(n+l)!) e^{-eta/2} eta^l L^{2l+1}_{n-l-1}(eta), eta = (2Z/n)(r/a0), a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2) ... n = 1,2,3,... ; l = 0,1,...,n-1 ... The corresponding discrete energy levels in the cgs units are given by Bohr's formula E_n = -m Z^2 e^4/(2 hbar^2 n^2) (3.5) ... they do not depend on the quantum number of the orbital angular momenta l due to a hidden SO(4)-symmetry'; p.10: '<r> = (a0/2Z)(3n^2 - l(l+1)) (3.15)'. Cordero-Soto & Suslov (0908.0032 p.2 eqs 2.6-2.7): Kramers-Pasternack recursion '<r^k> = 2n(2k+1)/(k+1) (n a0/2Z) <r^{k-1}> - k((2l+1)^2 - k^2)/(k+1) (n a0/2Z)^2 <r^{k-2}>' with '<1/r> = Z/(a0 n^2), <1> = 1'. CODATA 2022 (2409.03787 p.10 eq 26): 'E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1 + F) = -(R_inf hc/n^2)(1 + F), where E_h = alpha^2 m_e c^2 ... The dimensionless function F is small compared to one and is determined by QED, recoil corrections, etc.' With hbar = c = 1, e^2 = alpha, Z = 1: E_n = -m alpha^2/(2n^2), a0 = 1/(m alpha), <r> = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m alpha) -- identically excite.py:954-958.
published_hypotheses: nonrelativistic stationary Schrodinger equation for one electron (Suslov-Trey sec 3; Sec 1: 'nonrelativistic Schrodinger and relativistic Dirac wave equations for the motion of electron in a central attractive force field')

spinless electron: no spin-orbit / fine structure; Suslov-Trey p.16: the O(mu^4) term of (4.17) 'gives the so-called fine structure ... obtained in the Pauli approximation which includes interaction of the spin', i.e. outside the Schrodinger model

pure static Coulomb potential U = -Z e^2/r of a point charge (Suslov-Trey eq 3.23 'nucleus of charge Ze'; CODATA 'point nucleus'); no radiative (QED) corrections -- CODATA eq (26) puts QED, recoil and nuclear size in F

infinitely heavy nucleus: m is the electron mass m_e with a0 = hbar^2/(m e^2) (Suslov-Trey eq 3.3); CODATA eqs (28)-(30): 'infinitely heavy point nucleus', finite nuclear mass handled by the reduced mass m_r = m_e m_N/(m_e + m_N)
bound (discrete) states only: n = 1,2,...; l = 0..n-1; normalisable R_nl (Suslov-Trey eq 3.4)
Z general (hydrogen-like ion); hydrogen is Z = 1
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED FROM THE NAMED LIST (not from the model): 'nonrelativistic, spinless, no radiative/QED corrections' is not among the hypotheses named at excite.py:954-955 ('hbar = c = 1, point nucleus of infinite mass'). It is implicit in 'the Schrodinger problem' (excite.py:196) and in the canonical key's word 'Nonrelativistic'; the relativistic side is carried separately by dirac_level (excite.py:962-968, audited as dirac-coulomb-spectrum). D18 (excite.py:195-198) scopes its conclusion to 'Every dimensionless observable OF THAT MODEL', so the drift is a naming omission, not a use outside the class.

UNNAMED RESIDUAL for any application of D18 to REAL hydrogen: within QED at fixed alpha, muonic and hadronic vacuum polarisation carry m_e/m_mu and m_e/m_hadron (2602.14980 p.1: f_QED 'including muonic and hadronic contributions'; hVP moves nu(2S-6P) by 0.46 kHz of 730.69 THz = 6.3e-13). Neither ledger.py:514-516 ('alpha not held fixed (H1) or finite nuclear size -- the residual channels, O(eps) through m_p/m_e') nor specthm.py:1390-1391 names it. Magnitude ~1e-12 x eps; recorded, not a refutation.

LABEL DISCREPANCY (not a refutation): ledger.py:515-516 files 'finite nuclear size' under 'O(eps) through m_p/m_e'. Finite size enters through r_p/a0 (CODATA eq 50: (r_N/lambda_C)^2 (Z alpha)^2), not through m_p/m_e; computed here as (4/3) alpha^2 (r_p/lambda_C)^2 = 3.36e-10 of the 1S Bohr energy, scaling (1+eps)^3 instead of (1+eps). Both residuals are 'electron mass against a QCD-fixed scale', so the ledger's conclusion (a small computable O(eps) shift, never a rebinding) is unchanged.

ADDED BY THE TREE (scenario, not theorem): 'alpha fixed (H2)' (excite.py:195-196). The source treats alpha as a constant; the tree's H2 is the variation scenario under which the dilation is asked. Consistent with the source; under H1 the tree itself notes alpha moves (excite.py:202-203).
NARROWER, HARMLESS: hydrogen_levels (excite.py:953-958) hard-codes Z = 1; the source is general Z. --verify V8 (excite.py:1787-1795) keeps Z alpha symbolic.
MATCHES: 'point nucleus of infinite mass (clamped)' = CODATA 'infinitely heavy point nucleus' (2409.03787 p.11 eq 28); bound-state ranges n = 1..6, l = 0..n-1 (excite.py:956-957) = Suslov-Trey p.8.

rederivation.outcome: 33/33 PASS (exit 0; output in rederive/hydrogen-schrodinger-spectrum.out). (i) For every n <= 6 and l < n (21 states), the published R_nl (Suslov-Trey eq 3.2) satisfies the radial Schrodinger equation with E_n = -m (Z alpha)^2/(2n^2) exactly (residual/R = 0), is normalised, and gives <r> = (3n^2 - l(l+1))/(2 m Z alpha) exactly. (ii) CONTROL: a wrong level fails the eigen-equation. (iii) Kramers-Pasternack recursion (0908.0032 eq 2.6-2.7) at k = 1 gives the same <r> for SYMBOLIC n, l. (iv) CODATA eq (29) Dirac f(n,kappa) expanded to O((Z alpha)^4) for n <= 4, all kappa, equals Suslov-Trey eq (4.17): the Bohr level is its O(alpha^2) term. (v) The clamped model dilates exactly under m -> m(1+eps), eps in {1/10, -3/7, 1e-18}, with the tree's alpha as an exact rational. (vi) Data: alpha move 6.79e-10; real 1H ionization energy reproduced to the digits CODATA Table IV quotes once reduced mass, the Dirac alpha^4 term and the READ 1S Lamb shift are included; reduced-mass departure coefficient 1/(1+m_p/m_e) = 5.4432e-4; two-body model internal ratios mass-free; finite-size term 3.364e-10. A first run FAILED check (vi) because this auditor's own tolerance omitted the fine-structure + Lamb terms; that was an error in the check, corrected by adding the READ physics, not a discrepancy in the source or the tree. Box caveat: (i) is shown on n <= 6; (iii) is symbolic in n, l. Tree's own excite.py --selftest also run: SELFTEST PASS, D18 rows [ok].

later_literature.what: Real H levels are E = -(E_h/2n^2)(1+F) with F from Dirac, recoil, QED, nuclear size (eqs 26-64). The Schrodinger result is the F = 0, clamped-point-nucleus limit -- exactly the class excite.py names. Narrows real hydrogen, not the tree's model.

later_literature.ref: arXiv:2602.14980 (Maisenbacher et al., 'Sub-part-per-trillion test of the Standard Model with atomic hydrogen', Nature 2026)
later_literature.what: Eq (1): E_nlJ = -chR_inf[f_Dirac(alpha, m_p/m_e) + f_QED(... incl. muonic and hadronic VP) + delta_l0 C_NS r_p^2/n^3]; 2S-6P measured to 0.66 ppt, SM prediction agrees to 0.7 ppt; r_p = 0.8406(15) fm agrees with muonic. Confirms the Bohr term as leading order and names the non-dilating residuals (hVP ~6e-13).

later_literature.ref: arXiv:1807.08337 (Kozlov & Budker 2018, 'Sensitivity coefficients to variation of fundamental constants')
later_literature.what: p.1: 'The energies of all stationary states ... are proportional to the atomic energy unit E_h ... and additionally depend on alpha and mu = m_e/m_p ... nuclear radii'; 'we need to measure the ratio of two frequencies ... the dependence on the atomic energy unit cancels out.' This is D18's content (m_e is a unit) with exactly the tree's residual channels (mu, nuclear radii) plus alpha.
Closed forms for all <r^p> in the nonrelativistic Coulomb problem; eq (3.15) is the tree's <r>.

lacked_data: What Schrodinger (1926) lacked: electron spin in the wave equation (Pauli 1927, Dirac 1928), the Lamb shift (1947), the proton's finite size (1950s; radius puzzle 2010-2026), CODATA-precision alpha and m_p/m_e, and hadronic/muonic vacuum polarisation. Evidence that having them does NOT change the result as used: (a) the result is a theorem about a stated model -- re-derived exactly here (21 states, plus symbolic <r>); no datum enters its truth. (b) Every missing datum is exactly one of the model's hypotheses (nonrelativistic/spinless, no QED, clamped, point), and the size of each departure was COMPUTED: reduced mass 5.4e-4, fine structure alpha^2/4 = 1.3e-5, 1S Lamb 2.5e-6, finite size 3.4e-10, hVP ~6e-13 -- and together they reproduce the real 1H ionization energy to the digits CODATA quotes. (c) The move in alpha 2018 -> 2022 (6.8e-10) cannot move D18, which holds for every alpha. Evidence FOR M's hypothesis in this row: the later data do show the model is incomplete as physics of real hydrogen, and two residual channels relevant to D18 applied to real atoms are not named on the board (muonic/hadronic VP; finite size filed under the wrong ratio at ledger.py:515-516). Both are ~1e-10..1e-12 x eps and change no board conclusion. Verdict on M's hypothesis for this result: lacked data -> incomplete-as-physics (always known and named), not inaccurate or wrong as a theorem.
grade_evidence: Statement READ via restatement (0707.1887 eqs 3.5, 3.15; 0908.0032 eqs 2.6-2.7; CODATA 2022 eq 26 at F = 0) is identical to excite.py:954-958; the tree's named hypotheses (point nucleus of infinite mass, hbar = c = 1) match the source's, and its added H2 (alpha fixed) is a scenario consistent with it. sympy re-derivation 33/33 PASS: eigen-equation, normalisation and <r> exact for all 21 states n <= 6, Kramers-Pasternack <r> symbolic in n, l, Dirac -> Bohr limit, exact dilation. The only moved datum (alpha, 6.8e-10) cannot move an identity in alpha. The drift found is a naming omission (nonrelativistic/no-QED not in the named list; muonic/hadronic VP unnamed; finite size mislabelled 'through m_p/m_e' at ledger.py:515-516) -- the tree never applies the result outside 'that model' (excite.py:197-198), so none of these is a narrower class of use, and each is recorded as a discrepancy, not repaired.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if any owner (excite.py D18, ledger.py S7/D18, specthm.py SR4) is shown to apply 'EXACT dilation' / 'exactly null' to REAL hydrogen without the residuals (then the unnamed QED-loop channel at ~1e-12 eps and the reduced-mass channel at 5.4e-4 eps would be dropped hypotheses). A failure of the eigen-equation or <r> for some n > 6 would be WRONG -- but (iii) proves <r> symbolically and the Bohr formula is the O(alpha^2) term of the exact Dirac level for all n, so none is expected. No datum can make it DATA-DEPENDENT: the result holds for every alpha and every m.
